topics.label: Introduction to complement
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and introduces complement as a complex but essential immunological topic.

topics.label: Fundamentals and core mechanics of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the general architecture, nomenclature conventions, and central role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct upstream pathways that initiate complement activation on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the primary downstream effector functions executed by complement activation to eliminate pathogens.

topics.label: Regulation of complement activity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how deficiencies in individual complement components produce distinct clinical phenotypes and diseases.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens evolve mechanisms to circumvent complement attack and how these factors are used in medicine.

topics.label: Conclusion and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming topic on the adaptive immune system.
